column2: (Fronto-Parietal Network): The average signal across all FPN (also known as Central Executive Network) parcels. This tracks the overall activation of the large-scale network responsible for "online" task switching, sustained attention, and goal-directed cognitive control.

(Default Mode Network): The average signal across all DMN parcels. This tracks the overall activation of the network associated with the brain's "resting" state, mind-wandering, episodic memory retrieval, and self-referential internal thought.

(Salience Network): The average signal across all Salience/Ventral Attention network parcels. This tracks the network that acts as a cognitive "switch," detecting behaviorally relevant external or internal stimuli to direct attention.
(Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex): The primary frontal hub of the FPN. Functionally associated with working memory, planning, and abstract reasoning.

(Posterior Parietal Cortex): The posterior hub of the FPN (including the Intraparietal Sulcus and Superior Parietal Lobule). Functionally coordinates with the prefrontal cortex to guide attention and integrate sensory information.
(Dorsal Anterior Cingulate Cortex & pre-Supplementary Motor Area): The medial component of the FPN. Functionally associated with action-selection, conflict resolution, and error monitoring.
(Medial Prefrontal Cortex): The anterior hub of the DMN. Functionally central to self-referential processing, social cognition, and evaluating emotional significance.
(Posterior Cingulate Cortex & Precuneus): The central posterior hub of the DMN. Highly metabolically active during rest and broadly involved in autobiographical memory and consciousness.
(Inferior Parietal Lobule): The lateral parietal component of the DMN (specifically encompassing the Angular Gyrus). Functionally involved in semantic processing, reading, and memory retrieval.
(Medial Temporal Lobe): A distinct sub-system of the DMN that includes the Hippocampus and Parahippocampal Gyrus. Functionally critical for the encoding and retrieval of episodic memories.
(Anterior Insula): The primary sensory/interoceptive node of the Salience Network. Functionally maps visceral states (e.g., heart rate, gut feelings) and integrates them with emotional awareness.
(Anterior Cingulate Cortex): The executive node of the Salience Network. Works in tandem with the Anterior Insula to mobilize cognitive and motor resources once a salient stimulus is detected.
